title: Descent to a finite coefficient field; $\Dctf(X,\Qlb)$ as a $2$-colimit
statement:
The coefficient ring $\Qlb$ is a filtered union of the fields $E$, but integral lattices exist
only over a single $E$. We therefore show that every object and every morphism of
$\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is defined over some finite $E$. For $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$ and a finite
extension $F/E$ we write $C_F=F_X\otimes_{E_X}C$ and $C_{\Qlb}=\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}C$ for the
extensions of scalars, given by functors $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},F)$ and
$D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Qlb)$; since $F_X$ and $\QbarX$ are flat over
$E_X$ ([lem-sfb-subfield-flat], [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat]), these need no deriving.

Let $X$ be a standing scheme.

1. Every lisse $\QbarX$-module is isomorphic to $L_{\Qlb}$ for a lisse $E_X$-module $L$ and
   some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$.
2. For $C,D\in\Dbc(X,E)$ and every integer $r$, extension of scalars induces an isomorphism
   $$
   \varinjlim_{F\supset E}\Hom_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},F)}(C_F,D_F[r])\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
   \Hom_{D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Qlb)}(C_{\Qlb},D_{\Qlb}[r]),
   $$
   the colimit running over finite extensions $F$ of $E$ in $\Qlb$.
3. Every object of $\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to $K_{\Qlb}$ for some $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ and
   some finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$.

4. For rational coefficients $\Dctf=\Dbc$; these are the bounded constructible categories
   $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$ of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. By (2) with $r=0$ and (3), extension
   of scalars identifies
   $$
   \Dctf(X,\Qlb)\simeq\mathop{\text{2-colim}}_{E\subset\Qlb}\Dctf(X,E)
   $$
   as ordinary categories (in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]): every object of
   $\Dctf(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to $K_{\Qlb}$ for some finite $E$ and some $K\in\Dctf(X,E)$, and
   for $K,L\in\Dctf(X,E)$ extension of scalars induces a bijection
   $$
   \varinjlim_{F\supset E}\Hom_{\Dctf(X,F)}(K_F,L_F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\Hom_{\Dctf(X,\Qlb)}(K_{\Qlb},L_{\Qlb}),
   $$
   the colimit running over finite extensions $F$ of $E$ in $\Qlb$.

proof.text: The standing setting makes the structure morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ separated and of finite type. Finite type includes quasi-compactness. The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine and hence qcqs. The diagonal of $f$ is a closed immersion; over each affine open its inverse image is an affine $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, hence quasi-compact. Thus $f$ is quasi-separated by definition. Applying permanence (2) to $f$ and the qcqs base proves that $X$ is qcqs. This verifies the hypothesis of lisse descent without using any Noetherianity assertion.

For finite $E\le F$, the two flatness statements say that $F_X\otimes_{E_X}-$ and $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}-$ preserve finite limits. The source and target here are the abelian module categories underlying the cited derived categories, so finite colimits exist. Clause (2) of the current change-of-scalars statement therefore makes extension of scalars right exact, and these functors are exact. The exact-functor clause of the derived-categories statement identifies their left derived functors with their termwise functors. Consequently the scalar extensions in the item need no deriving, including on the unbounded ambient derived categories.

proof.text: By the preceding qcqs verification, part (1) of the existing lisse descent lemma applies to $X$. For every lisse $\QbarX$-module $L$ it gives a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, a lisse $E_X$-module $L_E$, and $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}L_E\cong L$, proving assertion (1).

Apply part (3) of the existing derived-Hom descent statement to the given $C,D\in D^b_c(X,E)$ and the given integer $r$. Its map $\varinjlim_{F\supseteq E}\operatorname{Hom}(C_F,D_F[r])\to\operatorname{Hom}(C_{\Qlb},D_{\Qlb}[r])$ is bijective, which is assertion (2). This is an isomorphism of groups because the canonical scalar-extension maps are additive. The index is the finite subextensions of the fixed $\Qlb$ containing $E$, including $E$ itself, and the cited statement is natural for their transition maps.

Apply the current bounded-object descent statement in its explicitly specified coefficient categories: $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ consists of bounded complexes with constructible cohomology over the pulled-back condensed ring $\Lambda_X$, inside the unbounded derived category of sheaf module objects. All finite fields are subfields of the fixed $\Qlb$, and scalar extension is the same derived coefficient change identified in Steps 2 and 7. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$ the statement gives a finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $K_E\in D^b_c(X,E)$ with $(K_E)_{\Qlb}\cong K$, precisely assertion (3). For every finite $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Qlb$, it also gives $(K_E)_F\in D^b_c(X,F)$ and $((K_E)_F)_{\Qlb}\cong K$, justifying the common coefficient fields used below.

For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, the coefficient-heart statement gives $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)=D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$. The bounded-constructible definition identifies these with $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$, full subcategories of the ordinary module-derived categories; their Hom sets are the ambient Hom sets. Thus assertion (3) gives the object clause in assertion (4), and assertion (2) at $r=0$ gives its displayed Hom-set bijection, with exactly the same scalar-extension maps.

Use the current coefficient-module conventions throughout: $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}=\Mod_{\Lambda_X}(\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab))$, where $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\underline\Lambda$, and $D$ is the unbounded derived category. In particular, the current definition of $T_{E,\Qlb}$ explicitly identifies it with coefficient change along the condensed inclusion $\underline E\to\underline{\Qlb}$; its source and target are $D(\Mod_{E_X})$ and $D(\Mod_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}})$. These are exactly the layer-B ambient categories in Step 2, denoted $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},E)$ and $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Qlb)$. The two derived scalar-extension definitions give $T_{E,F}$ and $T_{E,\Qlb}$, and the derived transitivity statement gives $T_{F,\Qlb}T_{E,F}\cong T_{E,\Qlb}$. The two preservation statements show that these functors take bounded constructible complexes to bounded constructible complexes. Restricting them to the full categories $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ and $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$ gives the restricted functors and their comparison isomorphism in the cited definitions. These are exactly the categories, functors, and isomorphisms specified by the constructible cocone definition. In particular all comparisons used below are the scalar-extension comparisons for this coefficient diagram. We specify the comparison witnesses directly from the tensor coequalizer in the change-of-scalars definition: $\theta_{E,F,M}$ sends $c\otimes(a\otimes m)$ to $ca\otimes m$, with inverse $c\otimes m\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes m)$. The balancing relations make both maps well defined and inverse, naturally in $M$. Apply them termwise and use Step 2 to descend to the derived categories, then restrict using preservation of constructibility. Thus we have constructed the transitivity isomorphisms used in this scalar-extension cocone, rather than inferring their formulas or coherence from the abstract existence of a natural isomorphism.

Check the three conditions in the filtered-two-colimit definition for the cocone of Step 7; write $\Phi_E=T_{E,\Qlb}$ and $\theta_{E,F}:\Phi_F T_{E,F}\cong\Phi_E$ for its comparisons. (Obj) is assertion (3), using Step 6. For (Hom-surj), take $K_i\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E_i)$ and $\varphi:\Phi_{E_1}K_1\to\Phi_{E_2}K_2$. Choose the finite compositum $H=E_1E_2\subset\Qlb$. To see its finiteness directly, the $\mathbf Q_\ell$-span of products of elements of bases of $E_1,E_2$ is a finite-dimensional subalgebra of $\Qlb$ containing both fields. Multiplication by any nonzero element is injective and hence surjective on this subalgebra, so it contains that element's inverse and is the compositum. Put $A=T_{E_1,H}K_1$ and $B=T_{E_2,H}K_2$, which are bounded constructible by Step 7. Define $\varphi_H=\theta_{E_2,H,K_2}^{-1}\circ\varphi\circ\theta_{E_1,H,K_1}:\Phi_H A\to\Phi_H B$. Assertion (2) at $r=0$ gives a finite $F\supseteq H$ and $h:T_{H,F}A\to T_{H,F}B$ with $\varphi_H=\theta_{H,F,B}\circ\Phi_F(h)\circ\theta_{H,F,A}^{-1}$. Let $\alpha_i:T_{H,F}T_{E_i,H}K_i\cong T_{E_i,F}K_i$ be tensor associativity. Its maps are $a\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto ab\otimes m$ and $a\otimes m\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes m)$, inverse by the balancing relations; these define maps of sheaf-module tensor products by their universal property, and then of complexes termwise. Exactness from Step 2 makes the same maps valid on derived categories. Set $g=\alpha_2\circ h\circ\alpha_1^{-1}$. The compatibility identity $\theta_{E_i,F,K_i}\circ\Phi_F(\alpha_i)=\theta_{E_i,H,K_i}\circ\theta_{H,F,T_{E_i,H}K_i}$ holds: by the tensor universal property, both sides send $c\otimes(a\otimes(b\otimes m))$ to $cab\otimes m$, termwise, and hence after localization. Substituting it in the formula for $\varphi_H$ yields $\varphi=\theta_{E_2,F,K_2}\circ\Phi_F(g)\circ\theta_{E_1,F,K_1}^{-1}$, exactly (Hom-surj). For (Hom-inj), let $g,g':x\to y$ in $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,H)$ have equal images under $\Phi_H$. Injectivity in assertion (2) at $r=0$ says their classes in the filtered Hom colimit are equal. In the disjoint-union construction of this set colimit, equality is witnessed by a finite zigzag identifying representatives with images at later stages. Choose a common upper bound $F$ for its finitely many stages by taking their finite compositum. Every generating identification becomes equality over $F$, so $T_{H,F}(g)=T_{H,F}(g')$. These prove (Obj), (Hom-surj), and (Hom-inj), and therefore assertion (4).
